finding: §8.4 gives a deliberate, byte-level compact accounting for exactly the fields this release adds or governs (harness_note/harness_stale stripped; next_action/nonblocking_open retained; accepted_open never emitted), but is silent on the existing mechanize_candidates array — which §8.2 branch 3 now couples to next_action by embedding the recurring class name inside the retained-verbatim `checks='[…]'` directive. On a --compact --record/--status response where branch 3 fires, the recurring class name is emitted twice: once in the mechanize_candidates array and once inside the next_action directive string. The release's own compact thesis ('strip what an agent does not need', 'worth one byte') therefore leaves an unaddressed redundant double-emission (or an unspecified strip) of the class precisely on the compact path it otherwise accounts for to the byte.

resolved.evidence: Accepted per the no-critical convergence policy (spec 0.31.0 §3-4, CLAUDE.md): no critical/high finding surfaced across 21 review rounds; this residual low AX-economy nit (mechanize_candidates compact fate) is an acceptance-level output-byte detail like next_action verbatim bytes (§10.7), not a spec invariant. Recorded in .tp-review for a future maintainer; deferrable to implementation/patch.

suggestion: In §8.4, state mechanize_candidates' compact fate alongside the other fields: either strip mechanize_candidates under --compact (the class is already carried by next_action's branch-3 directive when it is decision-bearing), or explicitly note that next_action's embedding of the class does not duplicate a retained mechanize_candidates array — so no class name is emitted redundantly under --compact.
